transitive.text: The verb takes a direct object (in Hungarian usually in the accusative, -t): *látom a házat* "I see the house".

intransitive.text: The verb takes no direct object: *alszik* "sleeps".

ambitransitive.text: The verb can be used either with or without a direct object.

ergative.text: The verb can be used with an object (someone does it to something) or without one (it happens by itself), like English "the door opened / I opened the door".

reflexive.text: The action is done to oneself, or the word refers back to the subject (*önmaga* "oneself").

reciprocal.text: The action is done to each other (*levelez* "to correspond with one another").

impersonal.text: Used without a real subject, usually in the third person: *illik* "it is proper".

auxiliary.text: A helper verb used together with another verb, e.g. *fog* + infinitive for the future, *szabad* "may".

copulative.text: A linking verb that connects the subject with a description: *van* "to be".

countable.text: A noun that can be counted and used in the plural: *egy ház, két ház*.

uncountable.text: A noun that is not normally counted or made plural in this sense (a substance, quality or idea): *víz* "water", *türelem* "patience".

not-comparable.text: An adjective or adverb with no comparative or superlative (no *-bb*, *leg-…-bb*): something either is or isn't, e.g. *halott* "dead".

comparable.text: An adjective or adverb that has comparative and superlative forms (*-bb*, *leg-…-bb*).

comparative.text: The comparative degree ("bigger", *nagyobb*), or a word naming it.

superlative.text: The superlative degree ("biggest", *legnagyobb*), or a word naming it.

plural.text: This meaning applies to, or is used in, the plural.

singular.text: This meaning applies to, or is used in, the singular.

plural-only.text: Used only in the plural in this sense.

singular-only.text: Used only in the singular in this sense.

in-plural.text: Has this meaning when used in the plural.

plural-normally.text: Normally used in the plural in this sense.

no-plural.text: Has no plural form in this sense.

collective.text: Refers to a group as a whole.

dual.text: Refers to a pair, or expresses "two-fold".

attributive.text: Used before a noun to describe it (as an adjective would be), not on its own.

predicative.text: Used after a linking verb such as *van* "to be", not directly before a noun.

adverbial.text: Used like an adverb, or relates to adverbs.

nominal.text: Used like a noun, or relates to nouns.

relational.text: An adjective meaning "relating to …", formed from a noun (often with *-i*): *felhasználói* "user's, relating to users".

possessive.text: Has a possessive ending (*-m, -d, -ja/-je…*, "my, your, his/her…"), or expresses possession.

personal.text: Relates to grammatical person (I, you, he/she…): a personal pronoun or a personal verb ending.

demonstrative.text: Points to something: "this, that, here, there" (*ez, az, itt, ott*).

interrogative.text: Used to ask a question: "which, what, who" (*mely, mi, ki*).

relative.text: Introduces a relative clause: "which, that, who" (*amely, ami, aki*).

ordinal.text: An ordinal number or word: "first, second…" (*első, második*).

noun.text: Used as, or forms, a noun.

verb.text: Used as, or forms, a verb.

adjective.text: Used as, or forms, an adjective.

conjunction.text: Used as a conjunction (joining words or clauses).

phrase.text: Used as part of a phrase.

particle.text: A small invariable word that adds emphasis or nuance; in science, a particle.

clitic.text: A short word that leans on a neighbouring word and is unstressed: *is* "also", the question particle *-e*.

participle.text: A verb form used as an adjective or adverb: *látó* "seeing", *látott* "seen", *látva* "having seen".

infinitive.text: The "to …" form of a verb (*-ni*: *látni* "to see").

with-definite-article.text: Used with the definite article *a/az* in this sense.

without-noun.text: Used on its own, without a following noun.

preterite.text: A past tense (in Hungarian grammar, the simple past).

subjunctive.text: The subjunctive–imperative mood: commands, "let …", "that … should" (*-j-*: *lássak, menj*).

definite.text: The definite verb form, used with a specific object ("the house"), or the definite article.

indefinite.text: The indefinite verb form, used with no object or a non-specific one ("a house"), or the indefinite article.

potential.text: Expresses ability or permission: *-hat/-het* "can, may" (*láthat* "can see").

causative.text: Makes someone do something, or lets it happen: *-tat/-tet* (*láttat* "makes visible").

frequentative.text: Expresses a repeated or ongoing action (*-gat/-get, -ogat*: *olvasgat* "reads a bit, now and then").

inchoative.text: Expresses the beginning of an action or state ("start to …, become …").

perfective.text: Presents the action as completed, often with a verbal prefix like *meg-* or *el-*.

imperfective.text: Presents the action as ongoing or incomplete.

passive.text: Passive voice ("is done"); archaic or formal in Hungarian (*-tatik/-tetik*).

nominative.text: The nominative case: the subject, with no ending.

accusative.text: The accusative case (*-t*): the direct object.

instrumental.text: The instrumental case (*-val/-vel*): "with, by means of"; also "instrumental" as in music.

ablative.text: The ablative case (*-tól/-től*): "from (a person or place)".

elative.text: The elative case (*-ból/-ből*): "out of, from inside".

locative.text: The old locative case (*-t/-tt*, found in some town names): "in, at".

prepositional.text: Relates to prepositions (which Hungarian mostly lacks; it uses postpositions and cases instead).

negative.text: Expresses negation, or a negative statement.

affirmative.text: Expresses agreement or a positive statement.

assertive.text: Makes a statement, as opposed to asking or ordering.

front-vowel.text: The front-vowel form of a suffix, used after words with *e, é, i, í, ö, ő, ü, ű* (vowel harmony): *-ben* rather than *-ban*.

capitalized.text: Written with a capital letter in this sense.

in-compounds.text: Has this meaning mainly as part of compound words.

in-certain-phrases.text: Has this meaning only in certain set phrases.

idiomatic.text: An idiom: the meaning of the whole is not simply the meanings of its parts.

formal.text: Used in formal, official or polite speech and writing.

informal.text: Used in casual, everyday speech; not suitable for formal writing.

colloquial.text: Typical of conversation rather than careful writing.

familiar.text: Used with people you know well.

slang.text: Very informal, often specific to a group or generation.

vulgar.text: Crude or obscene; offensive in most situations.

offensive.text: Likely to offend; often a slur. Avoid.

ironic.text: Used ironically, meaning roughly the opposite.

euphemistic.text: A softer, more polite way of saying something unpleasant or taboo.

mildly.text: Only mildly rude, offensive or strong.

childish.text: Used by or to small children.

literary.text: Used mainly in literature or elevated writing.

rhetoric.text: Used in rhetoric and the study of style.

exaggerated.text: An intensified, exaggerated form (e.g. *legeslegjobb* "the very very best").

excessive.text: An exaggerated or excessive form or meaning.

archaic.text: Old-fashioned; still recognised, but no longer used in normal modern language.

obsolete.text: No longer used at all; found only in old texts.

dated.text: Sounds old-fashioned; used mostly by older speakers.

historical.text: Refers to something that no longer exists, but the word itself is current (e.g. old offices or institutions).

neologism.text: A new word or new meaning that is not yet fully established.

proscribed.text: Used, but considered incorrect by style guides and teachers. Better to avoid in careful speech and writing.

nonstandard.text: Not part of the standard language; considered incorrect or substandard.

misspelling.text: A common misspelling. The correct spelling is given in the definition.

pronunciation-spelling.text: Spelled the way it's pronounced in casual speech ("eye dialect"): *lécci* for *légyszi* "please".

alternative.text: An alternative form or spelling of another word; see the word mentioned in the definition.

usually.text: Usually used this way, but not always. Qualifies the label that follows.

often.text: Often used this way. Qualifies the label that follows.

sometimes.text: Sometimes used this way. Qualifies the label that follows.

especially.text: Especially in this context or sense.

mainly.text: Mainly in this context or sense.

specifically.text: In a narrower, more specific sense.

rare.text: Rarely used. You will probably not need it.

uncommon.text: Not commonly used. (This is a Wiktionary usage label, separate from the "very common / common" frequency badges.)

figuratively.text: Used figuratively, not literally: *ég a keze alatt a munka* "work burns under his hands" = he works fast.

metonymically.text: Refers to something closely associated with it (as "the Crown" means the monarchy).

abbreviation.text: A shortened written form, e.g. *ld.* for *lásd* "see".

initialism.text: An abbreviation made of initial letters, said letter by letter.

acronym.text: An abbreviation made of initial letters and pronounced as a word.

clipping.text: A shortened form of a longer word: *gumi* for *gumiabroncs* "tyre".

ellipsis.text: A shortened form of a phrase, with words left out.

contraction.text: Two words, or a longer form, run together into a shorter one.

morpheme.text: A meaningful word part (a stem, prefix or suffix) rather than a whole word.

suffix.text: An ending added to words; in Hungarian, case endings, possessive endings and derivational suffixes.

prefix.text: An element added to the front of a word; for Hungarian verbs, a verbal prefix such as *meg-, el-, ki-*.

diacritic.text: An accent mark (like the acute ´ or the double acute ˝).

character.text: Refers to someone's character or nature.

dialectal.text: Used only in some regional dialects.

Internet.text: Used on the internet or in internet culture.

Greek.text: Relating to Greek mythology or ancient Greece.

Roman.text: Relating to Roman mythology or ancient Rome.

Jewish.text: Used among Jewish speakers, or relating to Jewish culture.

physical.text: In physics, or referring to physical things.

material.text: Referring to materials or physical substances.

noun.label: noun
noun.text: A person, thing, place or idea: *ház* "house". Takes plural and case endings.

verb.label: verb
verb.text: An action or state: *lát* "to see". Listed, as in Hungarian dictionaries, in the 3rd person singular present ("he/she sees") rather than the infinitive (*látni*); *-ik* verbs keep their *-ik* (*eszik* "eats").

adj.label: adjective
adj.text: Describes a noun: *szép* "beautiful". Comes before the noun and then takes no endings.

name.label: proper noun
name.text: A name of a person, place or organisation: *Budapest*.

postp.label: postposition
postp.text: Comes *after* the noun where English uses a preposition: *a ház mögött* "behind the house".

det.label: determiner
det.text: Comes before a noun to specify it: *minden* "every", *néhány* "some".

particle.label: particle
particle.text: A small invariable word adding emphasis or nuance: *csak* "just", *is* "also".

prep.label: preposition
prep.text: Comes before a noun (rare in Hungarian, which uses postpositions and case endings instead).

phrase.label: phrase
phrase.text: A fixed expression of several words: *jó reggelt* "good morning".

proverb.label: proverb
proverb.text: A traditional saying: *addig üsd a vasat, amíg meleg* "strike while the iron is hot".

contraction.label: contraction
contraction.text: A shortened form of one or more words run together.

suffix.label: suffix
suffix.text: An ending attached to words: case endings (*-ban/-ben* "in"), possessive endings (*-m* "my") and word-building suffixes (*-ság/-ség* "-ness").

prefix.label: prefix
prefix.text: An element placed before a word: verbal prefixes (*meg-, el-, ki-*) and word-building prefixes (*mikro-*).

interfix.label: interfix
interfix.text: A linking element placed between parts of a word.

character.label: letter
character.text: A letter of the alphabet. The Hungarian alphabet has 44 letters, including *cs, gy, ly, ny, sz, ty, zs* and *dzs*.

classifier.label: classifier
classifier.text: A word used when counting things of a certain kind (like English "a *head* of cattle").
